answer: Call it **Jittered Arrival Cadence**. Each identity must submit work in response to a signed, unpredictable timing challenge, and its arrival times must show natural jitter. Enforced at the summit of each epoch: bursty or lockstep submission is rejected. An operator running many puppets on one scheduler hits a marble boundary, since shared clocking collapses into detectable synchrony. Attacker cost: per-identity independent timing infrastructure reaching a stable zenith of entropy, not one cheap orchestration layer.
